analysis.title: Americas Real Estate: CRE Services: Diverging tones across CBRE, JLL & NMRK; Updating Estimates
key_insights: 3Q26 earnings from the three large CRE brokerages showed solid top-line results but different tones on 4Q26 and 2027 capital markets. JLL was most constructive, CBRE more measured, NMRK most conservative.

Open debates: whether JLL's 3Q26 beat and upbeat commentary reflect sustainable share gains, whether Newmark's 2027 framework (-10% to +10% EPS growth) is too conservative and sets a low bar, and whether CBRE's 2027 guidance was an apples-to-apples reduction if M&A was previously treated as upside.

JLL's CEO said debt and equity liquidity remain exceptionally high. Higher bond yields caused price recalibrations in US multifamily and moderated LTVs, but pipelines keep growing with minimal deal fallout. Management expects capital markets to grow in 2027. GS assumes 3% capital markets net revenue growth in 4Q26-1H27 and 4% in FY27.

CBRE said the September rate surge caused deal re-trades and delays. It projects capital markets flat through 1H27 and needs rate stability in 2H27 for improved growth. GS assumes -2% capital markets revenue growth in 4Q26-1H27 and 3% in FY27.

Newmark framed a downside scenario in which persistent rate volatility cuts full-year 2027 capital markets volumes 20% to 30% and adjusted earnings about 10%. GS assumes -5% capital markets revenue growth in 4Q26-1H27 and 1% in FY27.

Leasing: JLL raised its full-year leasing growth target to high teens after a +27% 3Q (US +39%). CBRE global leasing rose 6% (US office -2%, two large deals pushed to 4Q26) and it expects a low double-digit rebound in 4Q26. NMRK leasing rose 26.5% but it expects single-digit growth in 2027 on tight Class A availability. GS assumes 4Q26/2027 leasing growth of 8%/7% for JLL, 12%/7% for CBRE and 10%/8% for NMRK.

JLL's Real Estate Management Services margins are improving, helped by repricing of APAC property management contracts (one third repriced higher). GS assumes 3%/4% net revenue growth and 6%/7% EBITDA growth in 4Q26/2027, with 45bps of margin improvement.

CBRE's critical infrastructure services revenue rose 80% in 3Q, driven by the Pearce acquisition, which laps in November. With the pending Onnec acquisition, CBRE projects 2027 critical infrastructure revenue of $4.5 billion and total infrastructure-related revenue of $7 billion (>40% YoY growth).

CBRE Building Operations & Experience SOP growth is 14% in 4Q26 and 22% in 2027 (15% organic ex-acquisitions). GS models facilities management net revenue +7% in 4Q26 and +6% in 2027, with a one-time SOP hit in 4Q26 from contract restructuring. Project management SOP growth is 12% in 4Q26 and 15% in 2027.

NMRK's upside case (+10% EPS) already includes 1H27 capital markets pain and 2H recovery with double-digit Management Services growth. It matches the base cases of JLL and CBRE, so any rate stabilization plus broker recruiting and share gains could drive outperformance.

JLL announced an imminent $500 million accelerated share repurchase to complete by year-end, bringing FY26 repurchases past $1 billion, with net leverage at 0.5x. Management said volatility created an unjustified discount versus its Accelerate 2030 targets.

CBRE pulled back on buybacks in 3Q26 and will reduce repurchases further in 2027 to fund acquisitions with returns above 15%, mainly data center technical services such as Onnec. GS expects FY27 SOP growth of -24% versus 2026, including about $325mm of development gains.
NMRK reauthorized its $400 million buyback and is rotating capital from broker hires toward acquisitions in recurring Management and Servicing businesses.

GS estimate changes: CBRE 2026 adj EPS to $25.52 from $24.70, 2027 to $28.57 from $26.77, 2028 to $32.11 from $30.56. JLL 2026 adj EPS to $7.85 from $7.82, 2027 to $9.04 from $8.97, 2028 to $10.35 from $10.36. NMRK 2026 adj EPS to $1.84 from $1.94, 2027 to $1.94 from $2.17, 2028 to $2.17 from $2.39.
Price targets: CBRE (Buy) cut to $167 from $177, JLL (Buy) raised to $496 from $447, NMRK (Buy) cut to $17 from $19.

market_movers.rationale: PT cut to $167 from $177 on lower multiples (17.7x Q5-Q8 adj EPS, 11.5x EV/EBITDA) from market moves and updated guidance. Estimates are broadly unchanged, with added M&A upside.
PT raised to $496 from $447 after the 3Q26 beat and a stronger outlook. Multiples are 17.4x adj EPS and 10.7x EV/EBITDA.
PT cut to $17 from $19 as capital markets expectations were lowered. Multiples are 9.5x adj EPS and 6.2x EV/EBITDA.

sector_views.rationale: Solid 3Q26 top-line results across the big three brokerages, but management tone on 2027 capital markets diverges. Leasing and resilient outsourcing and data center infrastructure businesses offset capital markets weakness.

earnings_insights: JLL 3Q26: reported a strong beat and leasing revenue up 27% (US +39%). Full-year leasing growth target raised to high teens. GS raised estimates (2026 adj EPS $7.85 from $7.82, 2027 adj EPS $9.04 from $8.97).

CBRE 3Q26: global leasing revenue +6%, critical infrastructure services revenue +80%. GS 2026 adj EPS estimate $25.52 (prior $24.70), 2027 $28.57 (prior $26.77), 2028 $32.11 (prior $30.56). GS adj EBITDA 2026 $1,750.5mm (prior $1,716.4mm).

NMRK 3Q26: leasing revenue +26.5%. Management gave a preliminary 2027 adjusted EPS growth framework of -10% to +10%. GS cut adj EPS estimates to $1.84 for 2026 (prior $1.94), $1.94 for 2027 (prior $2.17), $2.17 for 2028 (prior $2.39).
risk_factors: CBRE: lower transaction and leasing volumes, reduced capital availability, slower resilient business growth.
JLL: less favorable capital allocation, lower equity earnings from real estate ventures, weaker capital markets growth.
NMRK: worse than anticipated capital markets recovery, weaker loan origination, less favorable capital allocation.
Persistent interest rate volatility could cut 2027 capital markets volumes by 20% to 30% (NMRK downside case).
vol_and_positioning: Rate volatility is the key swing factor for CRE capital markets. CBRE cited a September rate surge that caused deal re-trades and delays, and NMRK's downside case assumes persistent rate volatility.

tension_points.bull_case: JLL expects capital markets to grow in 2027 with liquidity exceptionally high and pipelines growing with minimal fallout. NMRK's upside case (+10% EPS) matches peers' base cases, so rate stabilization and share gains could drive outperformance.
tension_points.bear_case: CBRE sees capital markets flat through 1H27 after deal re-trades from the September rate surge. NMRK's downside case has 2027 capital markets volumes down 20% to 30% and adjusted earnings down about 10% if rate volatility persists.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Persistent interest rate volatility, or no rate stability in 2H27 (CBRE says it is needed to unlock capital markets growth).

theme_stances.key_argument: Brokerage tone on 2027 capital markets diverges, and Newmark's framework may be overly conservative, setting a low bar.
